advancedTraining.overview: Advanced arborist training covers professional-level climbing, rigging, cutting, jobsite flow, emergency response, and canopy strategy. This is the knowledge used by working arborists who climb daily and handle dangerous, complex trees.

advancedClimbing.description: Advanced climbing includes SRS movement, redirects, canopy transitions, limb walking, balance control, and efficient ascent systems.

workPositioning.description: Work positioning stabilizes you while cutting or rigging.

canopyTransitions.description: Transitions involve moving from one limb to another safely.

redirects.description: Redirects change rope angle to reduce friction and improve movement.

riggingTheory.description: Rigging theory covers load control, friction management, anchor strength, rope angles, and safe lowering.

negativeRigging.description: Negative rigging is used when cutting below your anchor point.

speedlines.description: Speedlines move branches quickly to a landing zone.

cuttingTheory.description: Cutting theory includes compression/tension awareness, hinge control, bore cuts, snap cuts, bypass cuts, and safe chainsaw handling.

stormResponse.description: Storm response requires identifying dangerous wood, tension, compression, leaners, uprooted trees, and unpredictable failures.
warnings: Hidden tension can cause sudden breaks

jobsiteFlow.description: Jobsite flow includes setup, communication, staging gear, crew roles, and efficient movement.

customerManagement.description: Customer management includes explaining the job, setting expectations, safety zones, and professional communication.

emergencyResponse.description: Emergency response includes aerial rescue basics, calling 911, stabilizing injuries, and preventing further harm.

efficiency.description: Efficiency minimizes wasted movement, plans cuts, stages gear, and uses proper climbing systems.

professionalGrowth.description: Professional growth includes certifications, continued training, gear upgrades, and building a reputation.
